extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematics students, instructors, and librarians looking for expository books or collections of elegant proofs
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and qualities used to judge or describe a mathematics expository book (readability, exposition style, selection of results, presentation, and originality). Relevant for readers selecting texts or authors preparing expository mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and broad-audience readability
rubrics_metrics.description: It is almost impossible to write a mathematics book that can be read and enjoyed by people of all levels and backgrounds, yet Aigner and Ziegler accomplish this feat of exposition with virtuoso style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the book can be followed and appreciated by readers with varying backgrounds (including non-mathematicians). Emphasises exposition that makes mathematical ideas approachable without requiring excessive prerequisite knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository clarity and entertaining style
rubrics_metrics.description: The style is clear and entertaining, the level is close to elementary, the necessary background is given separately and the proofs are brilliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for lucid, engaging prose that explains ideas clearly; a tone that entertains as well as instructs; organizing background material so the main exposition remains accessible; and proofs presented in a striking, insightful manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance and beauty of proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: This book illustrates ... what mathematicians mean when they speak about beauty. The proofs are brilliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferences for proofs that reveal surprising, clever insights or conceptual simplicity. Judges include aesthetic criteria (elegance, ingenuity) alongside correctness and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of fundamental, intriguing results and open questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad collection of theorems and their proofs that would undoubtedly be in the Book of Erdös. The theorems are so fundamental, their proofs so elegant and the remaining open questions so intriguing that every mathematician ... can benefit from reading this book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values choice of results that are central, illustrative, and that stimulate further inquiry by presenting open problems or connections; selection should serve both pedagogical and inspirational aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical design and visual aids
rubrics_metrics.description: This book is a pleasure to hold and to look at: ample margins, nice photos, instructive pictures and beautiful drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the book's physical and visual presentation — layout, margins, illustrations, figures and images — as contributing to readability and pedagogical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of new and original material in revised editions
rubrics_metrics.description: This revised and enlarged sixth edition features an entirely new chapter on Van der Waerden’s permanent conjecture, as well as additional, highly original and delightful proofs in other chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures whether new editions add substantive, original content (new chapters, new proofs, updated results) that justify revision and enhance the work's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level-appropriate background separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessary background is given separately and the level is close to elementary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether prerequisite material is presented in a separate, accessible way so that the main narratives/proofs remain uncluttered and suitable for the intended readership level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative expository credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are noted expositors (recipients of awards for mathematical exposition) with broad publication records in combinatorics, geometry, topology, and optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion that an author's prior expository accomplishments and reputation (awards, relevant publications) lend credibility and indicate likely quality of exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of rigor and elementary presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The style is clear and entertaining, the level is close to elementary ... the proofs are brilliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how the book balances mathematical rigor with accessible, often elementary-style exposition so that deep results are presented in a comprehensible, elegant manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness across specialties
rubrics_metrics.description: Every mathematician, regardless of speciality, can benefit from reading this book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the breadth of appeal and cross-disciplinary usefulness: whether the material provides insights or techniques valuable to readers from different mathematical specialties.
